# 2 Samuel Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 169r–170v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_002_page_001.jpg, 2SA_002_page_002.jpg, 2SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

**2:1** And-it-was after this, and-inquired David of-YHWH, saying, "Shall-I-go-up into-one of-[the]-cities of-Yehudah?" And-said YHWH to-him, "Go-up." And-said David, "To-where shall-I-go-up?" And-He-said, "To-Chevron."

**2:2** And-went-up David there, and-also his-two wives, Achinoam the-Yizre'elitess and-Avigayil wife of-Naval the-Karmelite.

**2:3** And-his-men who [were] with-him David brought-up, each-man and-his-household, and-they-dwelt in-[the]-cities of-Chevron.

**2:4** And-came [the]-men of-Yehudah and-anointed there David as-king over [the]-house of-Yehudah. And-they-told to-David, saying, "[The]-men of-Yavesh-Gil'ad [are the ones]-who buried Sha'ul."

**2:5** And-sent David messengers to [the]-men of-Yavesh-Gil'ad and-said to-them, "Blessed [are]-you to-YHWH, that you-did this-covenant-faithfulness [hesed] with your-lord, with-Sha'ul, and-you-buried-him.

**2:6** And-now, may-YHWH-do with-you covenant-faithfulness [hesed] and-truth [emet]; and-also I will-do with-you this-good, because you-did this thing.

**2:7** And-now, let-be-strong your-hands and-be sons of-valor, for [he]-is-dead your-lord Sha'ul, and-also me have-anointed [the]-house of-Yehudah as-king over-them."

**2:8** And-Avner son of-Ner, commander of-[the]-army that [was] to-Sha'ul, had-taken Ish-Boshet son of-Sha'ul and-brought-him-across to Machanayim.

**2:9** And-he-made-him-king over the-Gil'ad and-over the-Ashuri and-over Yizre'el and-over Efrayim and-over Binyamin and-over all-Yisra'el.

**2:10** A-son of-forty years [was] Ish-Boshet son of-Sha'ul when-he-became-king over Yisra'el, and-two years he-reigned. Only [the]-house of-Yehudah were after David.

**2:11** And-was [the]-number of-the-days that David was king in-Chevron over [the]-house of-Yehudah: seven years and-six months.

**2:12** And-went-out Avner son of-Ner, and-[the]-servants of-Ish-Boshet son of-Sha'ul, from-Machanayim to-Giv'on.

**2:13** And-Yo'av son of-Tseruyah and-[the]-servants of-David went-out and-met-them by [the]-pool of-Giv'on together. And-they-sat, these by the-pool from-this-[side] and-these by-the-pool from-this-[side].

**2:14** And-said Avner to Yo'av, "Let-rise, please, the-youths and-let-them-play [yesachaqū] before-us." And-said Yo'av, "Let-them-rise."

**2:15** And-they-rose and-crossed-over by-number: twelve for-Binyamin and-for-Ish-Boshet son of-Sha'ul, and-twelve from-[the]-servants of-David.

**2:16** And-seized each-man [the]-head of-his-fellow, and-his-sword in-[the]-side of-his-fellow, and-they-fell together. And-was-called that-place Chelqat ha-Tsurim [Field of-the-Flints/Sword-edges], which [is] in-Giv'on.

**2:17** And-was the-battle exceedingly hard on-that day, and-was-defeated Avner and-[the]-men of-Yisra'el before [the]-servants of-David.

**2:18** And-were there three sons of-Tseruyah: Yo'av and-Avishai and-Asa'el. And-Asa'el [was]-light on-his-feet as-one of-the-gazelles [tseva'im] that [are] in-the-field.

**2:19** And-pursued Asa'el after Avner, and-not he-turned to-the-right or-to-the-left from-behind Avner.

**2:20** And-turned Avner behind-him and-said, "Are-you that-one, Asa'el?" And-he-said, "I [am]."

**2:21** And-said to-him Avner, "Turn-aside to-your-right or to-your-left, and-seize for-yourself one of-the-youths and-take for-yourself his-armor." And-not was-willing Asa'el to-turn-aside from-behind-him.

**2:22** And-added again Avner to-say to Asa'el, "Turn-aside from-behind-me; why should-I-strike-you to-the-ground? And-how would-I-lift-up my-face to Yo'av your-brother?"

**2:23** And-he-refused to-turn-aside, and-struck-him Avner with-[the]-back-end of-the-spear to the-belly [chomesh], and-went-out the-spear from-behind-him, and-he-fell there and-died under-him [i.e., on the spot]. And-it-was, all who-came to the-place where fell Asa'el and-died, they-stood-still.

**2:24** And-pursued Yo'av and-Avishai after Avner, and-the-sun went-down, and-they came to [the]-hill of-Ammah, which [is] before Giach, [on the]-way of-[the]-wilderness of-Giv'on.

**2:25** And-gathered-themselves [the]-sons of-Binyamin after Avner and-became one band, and-stood upon [the]-top of-one hill.

**2:26** And-called Avner to Yo'av and-said, "Shall-forever devour the-sword? Do-you-not know that bitter [it]-will-be in-the-end? And-until when will-you-not tell the-people to-turn-back from-after their-brothers?"

**2:27** And-said Yo'av, "[As]-lives the-God, for if you-had-spoken [lit., unless you had spoken], then from the-morning would-have-gone-up the-people, each-man from-after his-brother."

**2:28** And-blew Yo'av [the]-shofar, and-stood-still all the-people and-not pursued again after Yisra'el, and-not added again to-fight.

**2:29** And-Avner and-his-men went through the-Aravah all that night, and-crossed the-Yarden, and-went all the-Bitron, and-came to-Machanayim.

**2:30** And-Yo'av returned from-after Avner, and-gathered all the-people, and-were-missing from-[the]-servants of-David nineteen men and-Asa'el.

**2:31** And-[the]-servants of-David had-struck from-Binyamin and-from-[the]-men of-Avner: three hundred and-sixty men died.

**2:32** And-they-carried Asa'el and-buried-him in-[the]-tomb of-his-father which [was] in-Beit-Lechem. And-went Yo'av and-his-men all the-night, and-it-grew-light for-them [at] Chevron.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — Achinoam/Avigayil:** These two wives accompanied David from his time in Philistine territory (cf. 1 Sam 25, 27:3). The narrator establishes domestic continuity alongside political transition.

**v.5 — hesed:** The word חֶסֶד (covenant-faithfulness) appears twice in vv.5-6. David commends the men of Jabesh-gilead for their *hesed* toward Saul's body and invokes YHWH's *hesed* upon them — a theological and political double move.

**v.14 — yesachaqū:** The verb שׂחק means "to play/laugh/sport," but the context reveals deadly combat. The euphemism is chilling — Abner proposes a gladiatorial contest using the language of sport.

**v.16 — Chelqat ha-Tsurim:** The place-name is debated. צוּרִים can mean "flints," "sharp edges," or "adversaries." The Masoretic pointing suggests "flints/rocks," but the context of mutual killing by swords suggests a wordplay on "sword-edges."

**v.23 — chomesh:** The term חֹמֶשׁ refers to the fifth [rib area], the abdomen/belly. The spear-butt pierced Asahel's midsection and exited through his back — a graphic detail preserved exactly.

*— EMET*
